key_insight: COP-GEN frames cross-sensor Earth-observation mapping as a stochastic conditional-generation problem and introduces a Latent Diffusion Transformer that produces multiple physically-plausible sensor outputs from the same conditioning input, avoiding deterministic collapse.
problem_solved: Non-injective relationships between optical, radar, elevation and land-cover modalities make deterministic mappings collapse to conditional averages; the paper addresses the need to model the full conditional distribution for realistic multimodal EO data synthesis and integration.
method: Encode multisensor Copernicus inputs into a compact latent space and perform generation in latent space to improve efficiency and fidelity.
Use a diffusion-based generative process combined with a transformer conditioning backbone to capture complex, multimodal conditional distributions across sensors.
Train the model to produce stochastic samples (multiple plausible outputs) for the same conditioning input, enabling uncertainty-aware synthesis and data augmentation.
impact: Provides a practical route for uncertainty-aware sensor fusion, realistic data augmentation, gap-filling and simulation in Earth-observation workflows, improving robustness of downstream ML tasks that depend on multimodal inputs.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: encoder → latent diffusion transformer → decoder, with arrows showing conditional inputs (optical, radar, DEM, land-cover).
Sample grid: multiple generated outputs for the same conditioning input to illustrate multimodality and diversity.
Uncertainty map: overlay or heatmap showing per-pixel variability across stochastic samples.
Data pipeline infographic: Copernicus inputs, training loop, and downstream use cases (augmentation, gap-filling, sensor translation).
paper_title: COP-GEN: Latent Diffusion Transformer for Copernicus Earth Observation Data -- Generation Stochastic by Design
paper_authors: Miguel Espinosa, Eva Gmelich Meijling, Valerio Marsocci, Elliot J. Crowley, Mikolaj Czerkawski
